newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore NTUC premium income grows by 30 percent.
newsitem.headline: Singapore NTUC premium income grows by 30 percent.

text.p: NTUC Income, one of Singapore's largest composite insurers, said on Monday that premium income for its life and general insurance business for 1996 was Singapore $744 million, up 30 percent.
In a statement reviewing its annual business results, it said single premium income for life insurance performed exceptionally well, achieving a growth rate of 123 percent.
Preliminary figures showed its total assets increased by 23 percent to over S$2.9 billion at the end of 1996.
Among new products launched by NTUC Income last year were the Travel and Cargo Insure-Line, a new way to sell insurance through the telephone with sales surpassing $2.5 million.
It also launched a new regular premium investment-linked policy in November, enabling policyholders to participate in a high return fund from as low as $100 a month.
NTUC also offered to waive fees for existing policyholders if they signed for a life policy in 1996. This resulted in the sale of another 12,000 policies during the promotion.
NTUC said motor insurance continued to dominate, accounting for 72 percent of its premium income. Its policies account for a market share of 33 percent in the Singapore private car sector.
